summary: Forest Service 40-foot wooden L-4 lookout about 3 miles west of Chemult, OR, built 1934 by a CCC crew; gone by 1965. No source describes the site today.

events.note: 40-foot wooden tower with 14x14 L-4 cab, built by a crew from the Odell Lake CCC camp; total cost $969.24
Fred Zumbrunn moved into the new tower in July 1934 and was its first lookout

Gone by 1965; these sources give no removal date or method

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1933-34 records and WillhiteWeb name the Deschutes National Forest; the Former Fire Lookout Sites register lists the Winema National Forest. The story reports both names.

notes_for_editor: Brief record lists the Winema NF; the 1934 sources say Deschutes NF. The Weebly page marks the tower 'Removed' with no date, so only the by-1965 bound is used. WillhiteWeb's 2022 photo is captioned only, so no current remains are described. Access level is left out because no source states public status; drive-up is recorded under visit. Revision 2026-10-09: the 15 Feb 1933 letter is addressed to a fire-protection association ('your protective area'), so the story says it was sent to the association, not written by it; the detection wording is 'excellent'.
